brand.name: TinyTab
brand.tagline: A lightweight window switcher for macOS

meta.description: Switch between windows with Cmd + Tab, including full-screen windows and other desktops. Jump with a single key. Connects only to activate, refresh, or deactivate a license, and collects no data.

footer.promise: Collects no data · Connects only to activate, refresh, or deactivate a license

common.copyFailed: Couldn't copy. Select the text and copy it by hand.

purchase.title: Buy
purchase.summary: One-time purchase: pay by QR code, then submit the email used for the purchase and the transaction number. Activate with a verification code once approved.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.summary: Reinstalling, new Macs, network and privacy, and the first-launch warning.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.summary: TinyTab connects only to activate, refresh, or deactivate a license, and collects no usage data.

home.intro: TinyTab switches window by window, across every display, desktop and full-screen space. Each window gets a letter taken from its app name: hold Cmd and press it to jump. Built natively in Swift, the installer is just 1.05 MB. It feels as native as a built-in system app.

windows.title: Window-level switching
windows.body: One row per window, most recently used first. Full-screen apps and windows on other desktops are one keystroke away.

hints.title: Single-key jumps
hints.body: Each window keeps its app-name letter while it's open. Hold Cmd and press it to switch; Dvorak and other layouts work too.

light.title: Light and focused
light.body: No search, groups or previews. It lives in the menu bar, never steals focus, and switches when you release Cmd.

offline.title: Quiet by default
offline.body: It connects to the license center only to activate, refresh, or deactivate a license. Otherwise it stays offline and collects no data.

steps.download: Download and install TinyTab (macOS 14 or later).
steps.pay: Scan one of the payment codes below. For USDT, you can also copy the address and send to it.
steps.submit: Enter the email used for the purchase (twice) and the transaction number below, then submit.
steps.activate: Open “Activate TinyTab…” from the TinyTab menu bar icon, enter this email, click Send Code, and activate with the six-digit code you receive.
steps.received: Once approved, you'll get an email notification.

purchase.methodsHint: The Alipay and WeChat Pay codes carry no amount. Enter {{cny}} manually when paying. For USDT, send {{usdt}} on the same network as the code; funds sent on the wrong network can't be recovered.
purchase.zoomHint: Click a code to show it on its own, larger, so your phone doesn't pick up the one next to it.

scan.alipay: Open Scan in Alipay and pay {{cny}}.
scan.wechat: Open Scan in WeChat and pay {{cny}}.
scan.usdtTrc20: Scan with your wallet or copy the address, and send {{usdt}} on the Tron (TRC20) network.
scan.usdtErc20: Scan with your wallet or copy the address, and send {{usdt}} on the Ethereum (ERC20) network.

order.title: Submit your payment
order.description: Fill this in after paying. Once approved, a license is opened for this email.
order.emailHint: Use an address that can receive mail: the activation code is sent there.
order.transactionNumberPlaceholder: Copy it from the payment details

transactionNumberHint.alipay: In Alipay, open this payment under “Bills” and copy the order number (订单号).
transactionNumberHint.wechat: In WeChat, open this payment under Me > Services > Wallet > Bills and copy the transaction number (交易单号 or 转账单号).
transactionNumberHint.usdtTrc20: In the wallet or exchange you paid from, open this transfer in your withdrawal history and copy the transaction hash (TxID).
transactionNumberHint.usdtErc20: In the wallet or exchange you paid from, open this transfer in your withdrawal history and copy the transaction hash (TxID), which starts with 0x.

order.submitted: Submitted. Once approved, you'll get an email notification. Then enter this email in TinyTab's “Activate TinyTab…” window to get a verification code and activate.

errors.emailMismatch: The two email addresses don't match.

errors.originNotAllowed: The site can't submit orders right now. Please contact the author ({{email}}).

notOpened.question: macOS says “Not Opened” and Apple could not verify it is free of malware when I open the download or TinyTab?
notOpened.answer: TinyTab isn't notarized by Apple, and macOS shows this for every such download; it doesn't mean malware was found. You see it twice, when you double-click TinyTab.dmg and the first time you open TinyTab, and both are handled the same way. Click Done to close the alert (not Move to Trash). Open System Settings > Privacy & Security, find the message under Security, click Open Anyway and enter your password, then open it again. It won’t appear after that.

reinstall.question: Do I need to buy again after reinstalling macOS or TinyTab?
reinstall.answer: No. Licenses belong to an email address; after reinstalling, get a verification code with the email used for the purchase and activate again.

newMac.question: What if I get a new Mac or the logic board is replaced?
newMac.answer: Activate on the new Mac with the email used for the purchase. At the activation limit, the new activation replaces the one that hasn't refreshed for the longest time.

network.question: Does TinyTab connect to the network?
network.answer: Not normally. It connects to the license center only to activate, refresh, or deactivate a license. Activation submits the email address, which is used only to identify the license owner and to send verification codes and order notifications. The license center stores the email, device model, and OS version, and collects no usage data. Everyday window switching is unaffected.

permission.question: Why does TinyTab need Accessibility access?
permission.answer: Intercepting Cmd + Tab and switching other apps' windows both require Accessibility access. It takes effect without restarting TinyTab.

network.title: Network
network.body: TinyTab connects to the license center only to activate or refresh a license, or to deactivate this Mac. Everyday window switching stays offline. If the license center can't be reached, an activated license keeps working offline; once the grace period ends, the app asks you to go online and confirm.

email.title: Email
email.body: Activation submits the purchase email. The email is used only to identify the license owner and to send verification codes and order notifications. The email and transaction number submitted on the purchase page are used only to check the payment.

stored.title: What the license center stores
stored.body: The license center stores the email, device model, and OS version (for example, MacBookPro18,3 · macOS 14.5) to identify activated devices. It never reads the computer name.

usage.title: No usage data
usage.body: TinyTab collects no usage data. The site uses no cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, or IndexedDB; a manually chosen interface language is kept only in the ?lang= URL parameter.

analytics.title: Site analytics
analytics.body: The site uses Cloudflare Web Analytics to count page views. It sets no cookies and collects no personal information.
